analysis:
The only change in this PR is in provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Helpers/MockCoordinator.swift, lines 445-456. `dropActiveWebSocket` now takes a configurable close code (default 1001) and an optional reason, and passes them via `.init(codeNumber: Int(closeCode))`. The default behavior is unchanged: it was `.goingAway` with the reason "mock dropping", and is now 1001 with the same reason. The purpose is to let tests inject a 1012 close, which models the edge's Conductor-change close.

This is a test-only helper. It is not part of the production provider binary or the coordinator. The mock binds to 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port and does not touch the Secure Enclave, App Attest, key custody, authorization or the prefix cache. No threat-model asset (A-001, A-003, A-008, A-015, A-016) or boundary (TB-002, TB-011) is changed. The T-041 definition was supplied as context, but this change does not touch the cache tier, TTL, scope or lookup-key derivation.

Remaining integration question: the production reconnect and resumption behavior on a 1012 close lives in non-supplied source. Whether the provider re-registers, re-runs App Attest resume and invalidates stale authorization on that close (T-053) is outside this unit. The mock only enables a test for it, so I found no regression here.
